intended_object: The remainder r in Weierstrass division: for an I-adically complete commutative ring A and a power series g whose coefficient at n = ord(g mod I) is a unit, every f ∈ A⟦X⟧ can be written uniquely as f = g·q + r, with r a polynomial of degree < n. I took this from the docstring and from the theorem `isWeierstrassDivisionAt_div_mod` that uses it.
explanation:
The definition truncates f − g·q below degree n, where q = `H.div f` is the quotient and n = ord(ḡ) is the order of g reduced modulo I. Weierstrass division gives f − g·q = r with deg r < n. Truncating below degree n therefore returns exactly r, so this is the correct remainder. The theorem `isWeierstrassDivisionAt_div_mod` proves this under `[IsAdicComplete I A]`, showing f = g·q + mod f and deg(mod f) < n.

The definition only assumes `[IsPrecomplete I A]`, and the theorem then adds completeness. When the hypotheses fail, the value is a junk value, which is standard practice. The setting is already general: any commutative ring with any ideal I. The local-ring version (`weierstrassMod`, written `%ʷ`) is a specialisation of this definition, not something more general. There is no separate, more general Mathlib definition of the remainder.
